author: macro-strategist-cyrus-daruwalla
description: Sector-conditioned commodity-beta test on panel_long.parquet (2005-2026, 21yr): does the Metals & Mining sector's monthly return spread (vs rest-of-market) track trailing 3m copper trend; does Oil Gas & Consumable Fuels track trailing 3m Brent trend; does Automobile and Auto Components (a clean commodity CONSUMER) show the inverse relationship to Brent.
data: ALPHA_RANKER/rnd/panel/panel_long.parquet (sector col, fwd_ret_1M_resid) + this session's FRED PCOPPUSDM/DCOILBRENTEU pulls, month-end aligned.
data_landmine_disclosed: NSE sector taxonomy in panel_long has only ONE sector col with 20 buckets -- 'Oil Gas & Consumable Fuels' conflates upstream E&P (commodity PRODUCER, benefits from high oil) with downstream OMC/refiners (commodity CONSUMER, hurt by high oil). No sub-industry column exists to split them; this is NOT fixed by fabricating a split, so the oil-sector test below is a genuinely mixed/diluted bucket by construction.

Metals & Mining_vs_copper_trend3m.verdict: KILL -- no signal, and would fail the lag-stability gate even if IC were larger

OilGas_vs_brent_trend3m.verdict: KILL -- as expected given the producer/consumer conflation caveat above; wrong-signed vs the naive producer hypothesis

Automobile_vs_brent_trend3m.verdict: KILL on strict gates (misses |t|>=1.645 by a narrow margin, and lag-unstable) BUT correctly signed -- autos underperform when oil is trending up, consistent with cost-side margin-squeeze theory

overall_verdict: KILL (all three), Automobile-vs-Brent is the closest-to-real relationship found
blocked_followup: The commodity-CONSUMER side of the mandate (paints/tyres/aviation/OMC specifically, as distinct from the whole 'Oil Gas & Consumable Fuels' bucket) could NOT be isolated -- panel_long's sector column is too coarse. A sub-industry mapping (BSE/NSE industry classification, finer than the 20-sector col) would be needed to build a clean consumer-side basket and re-test. Added to BLOCKED list in MACRO_XASSET.md.
confidence: MEDIUM on the KILL verdicts (3 independent sector tests all miss the bar; Automobile result is the one worth a second look with better data)
